framing_style.description: DIGITAL crop animation, not physical camera. Every shot is a crop window over an already-shot landscape source, blown up: ORB affine within shots gives rotation |r| <= 0.08 deg (shots 2-4) and strictly MONOTONIC scale; shot 2 returns exactly scale=1.0000 rot=0.00 tx=0.0 ty=0.0 with 400/400 inliers, which no handheld camera produces. Frame sharpness confirms it: Laplacian variance is 3.5-12.7 everywhere except the caption band (1013-1157), i.e. the footage is soft/upscaled while the overlays are crisp. The ramp is a slow ZOOM-OUT, not a push-in, and it is close to a house value: S1 -2.5%/s after its intro, S2 0.000%/s (frame-locked, ORB identity), S3 -3.0%/s, S4 -3.2%/s. S1 additionally opens with a fast eased zoom-out settle: scale 1.000 -> 0.862 over the first 0.33s (about -35%/s, decelerating) before joining the slow drift. The crop window also translates during shots (tracking/drift pan): S4 ty +222px full-res between n450 and n500, then -88px, i.e. it follows the speaker rather than sitting still. No shake, no speed ramps (mpdecimate keeps 605/615 frames, constant 60fps, no duplicate runs).

caption.position: vertical centre of frame - glyph bbox y=910..1019 px, centre y=963.5 = 50.2% of height (measured over all 615 frames, band located by full-height scan without assuming a position). Horizontally centred, cx 534-543 of 1080.
caption.style_description: One ALL-CAPS word per card, heavy bold sans (condensed grotesque, Impact/Montserrat-ExtraBold class), cap height ~100px = 5.2% of frame height, filled solid colour with a thick pure-black outline of about 10px (dark ring V~20 out to radius 10, softening to background by radius 16) plus a soft drop shadow. 22 cards in 10.25s = 2.15 cards/s. Cards hard-swap: the outgoing word disappears on the same frame the incoming word appears, no crossfade.
caption.color: THREE colours, and colour tracks WHO IS SPEAKING. white #FDFDFD (RGB 253,253,253) = the reaction/commentary host, 0.00-2.25s. hot magenta #F740F8 (RGB 247,64,248) = skit speaker A. yellow #FAFD08 (RGB 250,253,8) = skit speaker B. The exchange reads: A(magenta) 'WHAT MONTH IS TODAY?' / B(yellow) 'TODAY?' / A(magenta) 'YES' / B(yellow) 'I DON'T KNOW' / A(magenta) 'SEPTEMBER' / B(yellow) 'AH SEKTEMBER TODAY AH YEAH'. DECISIVE OFF-SCREEN TEST PASSES: at n=396 (t=6.600) the card 'SEPTEMBER' is magenta while the shot holds a medium framing of speaker B in the white shirt and speaker A is out of frame except for one arm - the colour follows the voice, not the visible subject. Colour flips are also co-timed with the cuts at 2.25s (white->magenta) and 4.45s (magenta->yellow).
caption.outline: black, ~10px solid at 1080 width (about 10% of cap height), plus soft dark drop shadow extending to ~16px
caption.animation: Per-CARD centre-anchored elastic pop with overshoot AND undershoot (damped spring, ~2 cycles). Measured as glyph bbox height normalised to the settled height, averaged over 9 cards (per-card starts 0.78-0.88, peaks 1.03-1.07 - highly consistent): f0=0.849, f1=0.958, f2=0.995, f3=1.018, f4=1.034, f5=1.048, f6=1.048, f7=1.028, f8=1.002, f9=0.979, f10=0.962, f11=0.956 (undershoot), f12=0.977, f13=0.969, f14=0.994, f15=0.999, settles 1.000-1.005 from f15. So: start 0.85, crosses 1.0 at f3 (50ms), PEAK 1.048 at f5-f6 (83-100ms), undershoot 0.956 at f11 (183ms), settled by f14-f15 (233-250ms). Anchor is the card centre in BOTH axes: cx is constant to +-1px through the pop and y0/y1 expand symmetrically about y=963 (920..1007 -> 910..1019). It is per-card, not per-word (every card is a single word, so the two are identical here) and not a full-frame composite ramp - the background is simultaneously scaling monotonically at -3%/s while the caption swings 0.85->1.05->0.96->1.00.

effects: composited SUBSCRIBE overlay top-left (YouTube-style pill + mouse cursor), t=0.000-1.283s: red 'clicked' state for frames 0-1, greys out from frame 2, fades to nothing over n65-n77 (1.083-1.283s). Rendered sharp over soft upscaled footage, so it is an editor-added overlay, not baked into the source.

full-frame RED FLASH at t=6.267s: mean R jumps 152->222 in ONE frame while G/B dip, then decays exponentially back to baseline over 19 frames (0.317s). NOT a cut - footage and framing are identical either side (verified on a labelled cut-pair sheet).
sub-bass impact sting co-timed with the red flash (20-60Hz band jumps from -53/-31dB to -13dB at t=6.30s)
slow continuous digital zoom-out on every shot (~-3%/s) plus tracking crop pan
hook: The whole first 2.25s is ONE uncut setup shot and it is a tee-up, not a payoff. A shirtless commentary host sits chest-up in a room of teal chairs, talking straight to camera: 'PRODUCTION / TO / THE / CLASSROOM / CLASSROOM / CAMERA / QUICK / SEE / SOMETHING' - i.e. he orders his own production to switch to the classroom camera so the viewer will see something. Nine white one-word cards fire in those 2.25s (one every ~0.25s), each with the elastic pop. A red-then-grey SUBSCRIBE button with a mouse cursor sits top-left for the first 1.28s. The frame opens zoomed in and eases out (scale 1.000 -> 0.862 over 0.33s) then drifts out slowly. The first cut - to the skit he promised - lands at exactly 2.25s, 22% into the clip, on the word 'WHAT'.
audio: Integrated -13.5 LUFS, LRA 13.9 LU, true peak +0.9 dBFS (clipped over full scale). NO music bed: 50ms-window RMS falls to -42.2dB in the gaps between words (t=3.30s) with 4-12kHz at only -33dB, which is room tone, not a bed - a bed would hold the floor up. Raw source dialogue for the first 6.3s, level -16 to -42dB. At t=6.30s, co-timed with the red flash, a loud sub-bass impact sting hits: 20-60Hz jumps from -53dB to -13dB and RMS spikes to -2.2dB, and from there the track stays hot (-10 to -16dB) to the end, so a sting/bed is layered in only from the punchline onward. No sfx on the 2.25s or 4.45s cuts.

Face detection was unavailable (no cv2.objdetect in this venv), so subject vertical position is eyeballed from frames rather than measured: the speaker's face sits at roughly 27-32% of frame height in every shot, with the caption at exact vertical centre below it.
